content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Thanks for kicking this off! Before we get into what the bookmark app should do, I'd like to understand the bigger picture behind it. That way we build something that actually fits how you work.

Let me start with the "why":

**When this app is finished and you're using it every day, what would be better than the way you handle bookmarks now?** For example — is the pain today that bookmarks get lost and you can't find them again, that they're scattered across different browsers/devices, that there's no good way to organize them, or something else entirely?

And a second question to understand the heart of it:

**Is "saving and managing bookmarks" the real goal, or is it a means to something bigger** — like being able to quickly find a resource when you need it, building a personal knowledge library, sharing collections with others, or keeping reading material for later?

Don't worry about any technical details yet — just tell me in your own words. Once I understand the goal, I'll confirm the direction with you, and then we'll walk through concrete screens together one at a time.

Right now my bookmarks become a cluttered pile, so I often can’t find something when I need it—or I forget why I saved it.

The bigger goal is a dependable personal library of useful links. I want to save a page quickly, organize it with tags and notes, search it easily later, keep a clear reading list, and archive things I want to retain without leaving them in my everyday view. It would also be reassuring to preserve a copy in case the original page changes or disappears.

**Your goal:** Today your bookmarks pile up into clutter, so you can't find things when you need them and you forget why you saved them. What you want instead is a *dependable personal library of useful links* — where you can:

- Save a page quickly
- Organize it with tags and notes
- Search and find things easily later
- Keep a clear reading list (things to get to)
- Archive things you want to keep but not see in your everyday view
- Preserve a copy, so it survives even if the original page changes or disappears

The underlying value is **trust** — knowing that anything you saved is findable later and won't be lost, and that clutter never gets in the way.

**Is that the right direction?** If anything is off or missing, tell me now.

And one more thing before we dive into the actual screens — **what kind of app do you picture using this as?** For example a web app in your browser, a mobile app, a desktop app, or a terminal/command-line tool? This helps me show you the right kind of working screens as we go.

I went with the opt-in flag because your goal was a calm everyday library, but I want to check: **should new links stay out of the reading list until you choose, or would you prefer everything new to start there?**

Duplicate detection handles the common variations correctly. Refresh **http://maker:4001** and let's walk through the three management flows one at a time.

**1. Edit address & description (not just the title).** On any card, click **"✎ Edit."** A form opens with **Title, Address, and Description** all editable. Change the description (and, if you like, the address), then **Save changes** — the card updates. This replaces the old title-only rename with full editing.

**2. Prevent duplicates.** In the "Save a link" box at the top, paste an address you already have — try `https://news.ycombinator.com` (Hacker News is already saved). Instead of adding a second copy, you'll get a notice: *"You've already saved this…"* with a **"Show it"** link that jumps to and highlights the existing card. Try a slight variation too — `http://www.news.ycombinator.com/` — it's recognized as the same link (scheme, `www.`, and trailing slash don't fool it).

**3. Delete permanently.** On a card, click **"🗑 Delete."** Because deletion is irreversible, you get a **confirmation** spelling out that the link and its saved copy, tags, and notes will be permanently removed. Confirm to delete, or cancel to keep it.

A few decisions I'd like your read on:

- **Delete is permanent and needs confirmation** — distinct from Archive, which just hides things recoverably. Is a confirmation prompt the right safeguard, or would you prefer deleted items go to a recoverable "trash" first?
- **What counts as a duplicate:** I treat two addresses as the same when they differ only by `http`/`https`, a leading `www.`, a trailing slash, or a `#section` marker — but a **different query string** (the `?…` part) counts as a *different* page. Does that match your sense of "the same link"?
- **Editing the address** keeps the existing saved copy, tags, and notes attached. Reasonable, or would changing the address mean it should be treated as a new page?

(In this demo that address keeps failing on purpose; a real transient failure would succeed on retry.)

**4. It still behaves like a normal bookmark.** Even in the failed state, you can open the original, tag it, note it, add it to the reading list, or archive it — it's a first-class saved link, just without enriched details yet.

- **On a fetch failure, the link is kept anyway** (with a warning + Retry), rather than refusing to save. My reasoning: losing the link would violate the "never lose it" trust. Is keeping-with-a-warning the behavior you want?
- **Non-addresses are rejected up front** with a message, rather than being saved as broken links. Is that the right call, or would you ever want to save a plain text note that isn't a link?

We've now explored the full picture — the core flows, the large-collection tooling, and the empty, oversized, error, and timing corners. Here's everything that's settled, in plain terms:

**Saving & revisiting**
- Save any page from a single address box; it's auto-enriched with a real title and short description, and the newest sits on top.
- Click a saved item to open the original in a new tab.

**Describing & organizing**
- Tag links (reuse your existing tags for consistency, or create new ones), shown right on each card.
- Add notes in simple Markdown, with a tidy two-line preview that expands.
- Rename or fully edit a link — title, address, and description.

**Finding**
- Live search across everything at once, plus precise queries: `#tag`, "exact phrases", AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, case-insensitive.

**Keeping a calm library**
- Reading list (opt-in) and Archive (hides links recoverably), as separate views.
- A preserved copy of every link so it survives even if the original changes or vanishes — readable content for pages, the original file for PDFs; a fixed snapshot you refresh only when you choose.

**Staying trustworthy & uncluttered**
- Duplicate-prevention when you save something already in your library.
- Permanent delete with a clear confirmation (no accidental loss).
- Sorting (newest / oldest / title) and safe multi-select bulk actions — tag/untag, read/unread, archive, delete — always scoped to exactly what you've selected.
- Friendly empty states, tidy handling of huge content, graceful errors for unreachable pages and non-addresses, and nothing that expires on its own.

That's **12 settled flows** covering everything from your original goal plus the management essentials you added.

I've noted a few polish items for later (how dates display, automatic retries, and the practical limits/storage of preserved copies) — none of which block building.
